PM (Marcus) owns: real sprint number + version, real US-/F-/E- IDs via story_counter, the freeze (prd_to_sprint.py + _freeze.py), sprint_lint, Rule 13 sign-off (Atlas), and dispatch. DO NOT overwrite offices/ralph/sprint.json. Proposed IDs US-386+ are placeholders.
_nature: This is an RCA sprint -- investigative, not code-complete. The root cause is a HYPOTHESIS (DriveDetector close/drive-end signal unreliable), not confirmed. Therefore the FIX story (US-388) is explicitly 'shape pending RCA' (US-387) per Watch List A-11: do not freeze a fix whose criteria depend on an unrendered finding. The in-process reproducer (US-386) carries the bulk and needs NO hardware; only the sprint-level IRL clause needs the car.

stories.title: Deterministic in-process reproducer for the DriveDetector close-signal defect (RED)
stories.goal: Build an in-process test harness that drives DriveDetector through the failure scenarios by feeding synthetic RPM / engine-on-off / timing inputs, and asserts CORRECT behavior -- failing RED on current code so the 28/29 defect (drive overlap + stale-open leak) reproduces deterministically WITHOUT the car.
acceptance: test feeds a synthetic RPM/engine-state sequence to DriveDetector for: (a) a short ~3-min drive, (b) two back-to-back drives ~1 min apart, (c) a key-on AFTER a drive whose close never fired
asserts: exactly ONE drive_id per physical drive (no overlap) AND each drive closes on key-off AND a key-on after a stale-open opens a NEW drive_id (no absorption)
the test FAILS (RED) on current detector.py, reproducing the 28/29 signature (overlap + missed-close)
Typecheck passes; the RED test runs and its failure is documented

validationCriteria.action: run the new reproducer against current detector.py

validationCriteria.outcome: two overlapping drive_ids minted (the defect), ids possibly out of temporal order

conditionalOutcomes: if the defect will NOT reproduce in-process at the detector level (manifests only with the real orchestrator loop / threads / timing), STOP and escalate to Atlas -- the reproduction strategy needs the real lifecycle loop, not just the detector unit

stories.title: RCA: root-cause the DriveDetector close / drive-end path
stories.goal: With the reproducer in hand, trace src/pi/obdii/drive/detector.py + orchestrator/lifecycle.py drive-start/-end/close logic and identify the exact mechanism: (1) why a drive fails to close, (2) why a second drive_id opens over an already-open one (ids out of temporal order). Document in an RCA.
acceptance: RCA doc names the exact code path + mechanism (file:line) for BOTH (1) drive fails to close and (2) a second drive_id opens over an open one
RCA explains the US-386 reproducer's RED behavior
RCA confirms OR refutes the Atlas hypothesis (defects 1+2 share one root = unreliable close signal) with evidence

validationCriteria.action: read the RCA against the reproducer
validationCriteria.outcome: mechanism identified, maps to the RED test, cites file:line

conditionalOutcomes: if the real root cause differs from the 'unreliable close signal' hypothesis, document what it ACTUALLY is -- do not force-fit the hypothesis

stories.title: FIX DriveDetector close-signal reliability (SHAPE PENDING RCA US-387)
stories.goal: Implement the fix so the US-386 reproducer goes GREEN: one drive_id per physical drive, every drive closes on key-off, a stale-open drive cannot absorb a later key-on. The exact change shape depends on the US-387 RCA -- this story is frozen as 'shape pending ruling, build blocked until RCA' per Watch List A-11.
acceptance: no overlapping drive_ids in the back-to-back scenario
a key-on after a missed close opens a NEW drive_id (no 8-day-leak absorption)
existing DriveDetector + lifecycle tests stay green
if the change is load-bearing, specs/architecture.md DriveDetector section updated in-sprint (Atlas design-gate DoD)

validationCriteria.action: pytest the US-386 reproducer + the existing detector/lifecycle suites

validationCriteria.outcome: one drive_id each, all close, no absorption

conditionalOutcomes: BUILD BLOCKED until US-387 RCA is accepted by Atlas -- do not start coding before the root cause is rendered
if the RCA reveals the fix is architectural (e.g. id-minting concurrency, detector re-entrancy), route back to Atlas for a design ruling BEFORE coding

stories.title: Regression lock + server-tripwire backstop confirmation
stories.goal: Lock the reproducer into the regression suite/manifest, and confirm the V0.28.0 server tripwire (detect_overlapping_drives) still flags any residual overlap -- belt-and-suspenders so a future Pi regression is still caught server-side.
acceptance: US-386 reproducer added to the fast suite / regression manifest (permanent)
a server-side test confirms detect_overlapping_drives still stamps data_quality=attribution_anomaly on a synthetic overlap

validationCriteria.action: pytest fast suite including the reproducer

validation.validationMethod: RCA + fix for the REOPENED A-9 DriveDetector close-signal defect (drives 28/29). The in-process reproducer (US-386) is the deterministic gate for the fix and needs no hardware. The fix (US-388) is build-blocked on the RCA (US-387) per A-11. The sprint-level IRL clause is the true acceptance gate -- a SHORT/BACK-TO-BACK drive pair + a key-on-after-missed-close (the exact scenario the single drive-27 PASS missed). The V0.28.0 server tripwire remains the backstop, so this is NOT a chain/deploy block -- an honest flagged record already exists for 28/29.
